answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money — sparingly and against verified performance — so Sybil inflation is filtered before it compounds. Tending a island, watching a vertex, and naming a harbor is the rhythm of earning trust — deliberately, repeatably, and never in bulk.
